p.i: Arma assueta capit, flexumq; à cornibus arcum
Tendit, & illa suo toties cum pectore iuncta

main_text.head: Epodus 2.versuum 15.
main_text.p: QVid post mortem Coronidis confecutum sit: quo-modo exemptus Æsculapius & Chironi erudiendus sit traditus.
Ἀλλ' ἐπὶ τείχει[?].) Consequentia mortis sunt sepultura, rogus apud veteres. τεῖχος ξύλινον vocat πυρκαϊὰν[?], rogum. sic σέλας Ἀφαίστου ignis ardentis periphrasis.
Τὸν ἔειπεν Ἀπόλλων[?].) Alterum ἐπιμύρον[?], commiseratio paterna, & quomodo Æsculapium ex flammis eripuerit.
Οὔνεκα [illegible, ~8 letters].) μίμησις patris condolentis affectum exprimens: sic Ovidius.

p.i: Non tulit in cineres labi sua Phœbus eosdem Semina: sed natum flammis uteroque parentis Eripuit.

main_text.p: Βάμματι δ' ἐν πρώτῳ[?].) Seruatur Æsculapius ex igni: mirum autem facit Apollinem vno βήματι[?] ex Pythone urbe in Laceria transiisse. Aristarchus hic legit τετράτῳ[?], quòd tres passus fecerit.

Καὶ ῥά μιν[?].) Duo praecipuè hactenus de Æsculapio docuit, genus maternum, cuius occasione fatum & calamitates matris exposuit: alterum nativitatem mirabilem Æsculapij, mortua matre ex utero & flammis eripitur. Tertio iam docet, quis illi datus praeceptor, Centaurus Magnesius, hoc est, Chiron Thessalus: sic Ovid.

p.i: Eripuit geminiq; tulit Chironis in antrum.

main_text.p: recte autem νόσις vocat πολυπήμονας[?], h.e. πολλῶν τῶν πημάτων[?].
main_text.head: Strophe 3.versuum 13.
main_text.p: QVantus professione effectus fuerit Æsculapius, quos morbos curarit, & quomodo curarit, hæc Strophe edocet.

Τῆς μὲν ὧν[?].) Quartus locus de professione medica, in qua quantus extiterit Aesculapius docet: quatuor praecipua recenset morborum genera: αὐτόφυτα ἕλκη, innata vlcera, vt cancer: secundo τραύματα quae ferro fiunt: tertio, βολὴ iactus, vt lapide, fuste, plaga incussa: quarto καύσεις, vt fe-brium

page.notes: Several Greek words are uncertain because the scan is faint and small; they are marked [?]. The Greek line after "Οὔνεκα" could not be read letter by letter and is marked illegible. The running text ends mid-word ("fe-brium") at the foot of the page, so the paragraph continues on the next page. Long s is transcribed as plain s throughout (e.g. "eosdem", "sed", "sua"), and u/v is normalised as specified; printed spellings such as "Thessalus" and "Ovidius" are otherwise kept as printed. The opening verse block is treated as the continuation of a stanza from the previous page.
